subtitle: How a Gajapati Carved Harmony in Stone and Poured it into Water

panels.shot: majestic wide shot of Kapilendra Deva standing between a rising temple shikhara and a vast ritual tank under construction
panels.action: Kapilendra Deva stands on a half-built ghat, one hand resting on a carved stone block, the other pointing toward a towering rekha deula silhouette and a broad, shimmering tank basin where Odishan silpis and labourers work in the golden light.

dialogue.text: In fifteenth‑century Kalinga, Gajapati Kapilendra Deva, a Vaishnava king, raised a Shaiva shrine and a vast tank, binding his realm with stone, water and shared sacred ground.

i18n.hi: पंद्रहवीं सदी के कलिंग में वैष्णव गजपति कपिलेन्द्र देव ने शिव मंदिर और बड़ा टैंक बनाकर, अपने राज्य को पत्थर, पानी और साझा पवित्र धरती से जोड़ा।

panels.shot: slow push-in on Kapilendra Deva in court, maps and temple drawings spread before him
panels.action: Inside a high-pillared royal hall, Kapilendra Deva leans over palm-leaf plans showing a rekha deula and a tank, while silpis and officers stand respectfully with rolled drawings and measuring cords.

dialogue.text: Kapilendra Deva, founder of the Suryavamsi Gajapatis, ruled a widening empire from Cuttack, his devotion resting on Jagannath, yet his gaze now fixed on Bhubaneswar and Puri.

i18n.hi: सूर्यवंशी गजपति वंश के संस्थापक कपिलेन्द्र देव कटक से फैलते साम्राज्य पर राज करते, भक्ति जगन्नाथ पर, नज़र अब भुवनेश्वर और पुरी पर।

panels.shot: medium shot of Kapilendra in discussion with a senior silpi holding temple elevation sketches
panels.action: Kapilendra sits on a low throne, listening intently as an elderly Odishan silpi kneels with a palm-leaf elevation of a rekha deula, intricate mouldings etched in fine lines, while younger craftsmen watch in tense silence.

dialogue.text: His forebears had inherited the tall deulas of Kalinga. Now, under his seal, new shrines and works would rise, echoing old forms yet marking a new royal line.

i18n.hi: पूर्वजों ने ऊँचे देउला पाए थे, पर अब उसकी मोहर से नए मंदिर और काम उठने लगे, पुराने रूप दोहराते, पर नई राजवंश की पहचान बनाते।

panels.shot: wide establishing shot of Bhubaneswar’s sacred landscape with multiple temple towers in the distance
panels.action: From a rocky rise, Kapilendra and a group of silpis look across Bhubaneswar, where older temple shikharas pierce the sky, the city’s groves and tanks glinting in the afternoon haze.

dialogue.text: Bhubaneswar’s skyline already bristled with ancient towers. Muktesvara, Rajarani, Lingaraja—older shrines whispered of bygone dynasties Kapilendra did not claim as his own.

i18n.hi: भुवनेश्वर का गगन पहले से ही प्राचीन शिखरों से भरा था; मुक्तेश्वर, राजारानी, लिंगराज—पुराने मंदिर पिछली राजाओं की फुसफुसाहट थे, जिन पर कपिलेन्द्र का दावा नहीं था।

panels.shot: focus on a specific temple site marked out with ropes and pegs
panels.action: At a cleared plot, ropes and wooden pegs outline the future Kapilesvara temple, as silpis kneel, tracing lines on the earth, while Kapilendra stands at the edge, hands folded, head bowed toward the site.

dialogue.text: Here, near the older shrines, his builders marked ground for Kapilesvara Siva. The inscriptions and fabric would later reveal a Gajapati hand in its making.

i18n.hi: इन पुराने मंदिरों के पास ही राज-मिस्त्रियों ने कपिलेश्वर शिव के लिए ज़मीन नापी; बाद की लिखाइयाँ और संरचना ने साफ़ गजपति की छाप दिखा दी।

panels.shot: low-angle close-up of carved stone block being raised, temple tower in early stages
panels.action: A heavy, sculpted stone block with lotus and scroll motifs is hauled upward by ropes and a wooden crane, with a partially built rekha deula core rising behind, Kapilendra watching from scaffolding.

dialogue.text: Stone by stone, the Kapilesvara deula climbed. Donaldson would later see in it the old Kalinga vocabulary, carried into the Suryavamsi age without breaking rhythm.

i18n.hi: पत्थर पर पत्थर चढ़कर कपिलेश्वर देउला उठता गया; बाद में डोनाल्डसन ने इसमें वही पुराना कलिंग शैली देखी, जो सूर्यवंशी युग में भी बिना टूटे चली आई।

panels.shot: medium shot at eye level of Kapilendra speaking quietly with a Shaiva priest near the construction
panels.action: Under a temporary canopy beside the rising shrine, a Shaiva priest with rudraksha beads speaks with Kapilendra, who holds his Vaishnava emblems yet listens with calm attention, silpis chiseling in the background.

dialogue.speaker: Kapilendra Deva
dialogue.text: If Jagannath is pleased, why should Mahesvara want for a roof?

i18n.hi: अगर जगन्नाथ प्रसन्न हैं, तो महेश्वर छत को क्यों तरसे?

dialogue.text: A king devoted to Jagannath now funded a Shaiva sanctum. His court moved between images, priests and maths, turning sect into shared protection, not rivalry.

i18n.hi: जगन्नाथ-भक्त राजा ने अब शैव देवल का खर्च उठाया; दरबार मूर्तियों, पुजारियों और मठों के बीच घूमता, सम्प्रदाय को टकराव नहीं, साझा रक्षा बनाता।

panels.shot: wide shot of completed Kapilesvara temple amidst trees, pilgrims approaching
panels.action: The finished Kapilesvara Siva Temple stands in full rekha deula form, its curving tower banded with mouldings, smaller shrines clustered around, as villagers and brahmanas walk toward its gateway beneath rustling trees.

dialogue.text: When Kapilesvara stood complete, its tower did not shout novelty. It spoke continuity—Kalinga stonework flowing on under a new royal sponsor.

i18n.hi: जब कपिलेश्वर पूरा खड़ा हुआ, उसका शिखर नई चाल से नहीं चिल्लाया; उसने निरंतरता बोली—कलिंग की पत्थरकारी नई राज-छत्र में भी बहती रही।

panels.shot: transition shot to Puri coastline and Jagannath temple in distance, then pan toward open low-lying land
panels.action: A sweeping view runs from the massive Jagannath temple rising above Puri’s roofs to a flat stretch of low-lying land outside, where Kapilendra and engineers survey with staffs and measuring ropes.

dialogue.text: At Puri, the great Jagannath temple, older than the Suryavamsis, already anchored coastal faith. Kapilendra did not build its core; instead, he looked outward—to water.

i18n.hi: पुरी में पुराना जगन्नाथ मंदिर, सूर्यवंशियों से भी पुराना, पहले से ही तट की आस्था का ध्रुव था; कपिलेन्द्र ने उसका गर्भ नहीं उठाया, वह नज़र बाहर—पानी पर ले गए।

panels.shot: bird’s-eye view of early excavation of Narendra tank, lines of workers defining the basin
panels.action: From above, long lines of labourers dig and carry earth, shaping a vast rectangular basin, while silpis stake out ghats and islands, Kapilendra’s officials noting levels on palm leaves.

dialogue.text: Here the court planned Narendra tank, a great ritual reservoir. Not just a pond, but a stage of water for Jagannath’s journeys and the city’s thirst.

i18n.hi: यहीं दरबार ने नरेन्द्र टैंक की योजना बनाई—एक विशाल तीर्थ-सरोवर; सिर्फ़ पोखर नहीं, जगन्नाथ की यात्रा और शहर की प्यास के लिए जल-मंच।

panels.shot: medium shot of silpis drafting ghat steps and island shrine, tools and scale models around
panels.action: In a shaded shed, Odishan silpis sit around a clay model of the tank, etching miniature ghats, a central island pavilion and stepped banks, while a younger craftsman measures with a string, lips moving as he calculates.

dialogue.text: Silpis who knew stone now thought in water lines. Steps, ghats, islands—planned with the same precision as a deula, but for boats, processions and tides of people.

i18n.hi: जो शिल्पी पत्थर में सोचते थे, अब पानी की रेखाओं में सोचने लगे; सीढ़ियाँ, घाट, टापू—देउला जैसी बारीकी से, पर नावों, जुलूसों और जनलहरों के लिए।

panels.shot: low-angle shot of massive stone ghat steps being set, with canal channel visible
panels.action: Men maneuver huge stone blocks into place to form broad ghat steps, while a newly cut channel guides water toward the growing tank, Kapilendra standing quietly as the first trickle arrives.

dialogue.text: Narendra’s ghats took shape in stone. Channels were cut so that when the monsoon came, the basin would fill, turning engineering into ritual lake.

i18n.hi: नरेन्द्र के घाट पत्थर में ढलते गए; नालियाँ काटी गईं कि मानसून में ताल भर उठे, इंजीनियरिंग खुद को अनुष्ठानिक झील में बदल दे।

panels.shot: dramatic wide shot of Chandan Yatra on the filled tank, boats carrying deities
panels.action: The full Narendra tank mirrors the sky, boats decorated with canopies gliding across, carrying small images of Jagannath in Chandan Yatra, while crowds throng the ghats and priests chant from the banks.

dialogue.text: Soon Chandan Yatra found a new body. On Narendra’s waters, Jagannath’s images sailed, the king’s hydraulic work becoming sacred route and festival ground.

i18n.hi: जल्द ही चन्दन यात्रा को नया शरीर मिला; नरेन्द्र के जल पर जगन्नाथ की प्रतिमाएँ तैरने लगीं, राजा का जल-कार्य ही पवित्र मार्ग और उत्सव-भूमि बन गया।

panels.shot: medium shot of Kapilendra watching the boats from a shaded pavilion, mixing officials and devotees
panels.action: From a pillared pavilion overlooking the tank, Kapilendra watches boats drift by, flanked by courtiers and soldiers, as commoners press together on the ghats, some bathing, others craning to see the deities.

dialogue.speaker: Kapilendra Deva
dialogue.text: Let them say the king built more than walls of fort and tax.

i18n.hi: कहने दें, इस राजा ने सिर्फ़ किले और कर की दीवारें नहीं उठाईं।

dialogue.text: The tank fed ritual and body alike. Its steps bore dancers and drummers, priests and merchants, weaving economy and piety in the same space.

i18n.hi: इस टैंक ने देह और देव दोनो को पोसा; इसकी सीढ़ियाँ पर नर्तक, ढोलिए, पुजारी, बनिए चले, एक ही जगह में रोज़ी और भक्ति को बुनते हुए।

panels.shot: intimate shot of an Odissi dancer practising near a temple, with Donaldson and Kothari’s perspectives implied in narration
panels.action: In the courtyard of an Odishan temple, an Odissi dancer practises a pose before the sculpted walls, while musicians sit nearby with mardala and manjira, the temple’s carvings echoing her stance.

dialogue.text: Such temples and tanks framed a culture of performance. Later, scholars like Donaldson and Kothari would trace how sculpture and dance answered each other in these sacred precincts.

i18n.hi: ऐसे मंदिर और टैंक ने प्रदर्शन की संस्कृति को घेरा; बाद में डोनाल्डसन, कोठारी जैसे विद्वानों ने देखा कैसे मूर्ति और नृत्य इन पवित्र चौहद्दियों में एक-दूसरे को जवाब देते हैं।

panels.shot: time-lapse style composite showing seasons changing over Kapilesvara temple and Narendra tank
panels.action: A blended scene shows Kapilesvara’s tower and Narendra’s ghats through sun, rain and mist, farmers, pilgrims and kings changing in dress and number while the stone and water remain constant.

dialogue.text: Dynasties would pass, names fade from court lists. Yet Kapilesvara’s rekha and Narendra’s waters held their lines, serving new generations without asking who first paid for them.

i18n.hi: राजवंश गुजर गए, दरबार की सूचियों से नाम मिट गए; पर कपिलेश्वर की रेखा और नरेन्द्र का जल अपनी लकीर थामे, नई पीढ़ियों की सेवा करते रहे, बिना पूछे कि पहली नेमत किसने दी थी।

panels.shot: present-day wide shot of Kapilesvara temple and Narendra tank with modern visitors, ghosted image of Kapilendra in the sky
panels.action: Modern visitors in simple clothes walk around Kapilesvara and sit on Narendra’s ghats, as a faint, translucent image of Kapilendra and his silpis looks on from the clouds above.

dialogue.text: Today, conservation reports refine dates and details, but the broad truth holds: a Vaishnava Gajapati sponsored Shaiva stone and ritual water, turning rule into shared space that still gathers people in his long-quiet name.

i18n.hi: आज संरक्षण की रिपोर्टें तारीख़ें और बारीकियाँ ठीक करती हैं, पर बड़ी बात वही है—एक वैष्णव गजपति ने शैव पत्थर और अनुष्ठानिक जल को निधि दी, राजकाज को साझा जगह बना दिया, जो आज भी लोगों को उसके बहुत पहले थमे नाम पर जोड़ती है।

title_i18n.en: Kapilendra Builds in Stone and Water

subtitle_i18n.en: How a Gajapati Carved Harmony in Stone and Poured it into Water
subtitle_i18n.hi: एक गजपति ने पत्थर से सुर गढ़े, पानी में उंडेल दिए
